findings.issue: onFullyRefunded does not check coin_return_reversals. The new handler counts a legacy earn-<orderId> row as prior, but the reverse is not true. If a per-return partial reversal is recorded and the completing return then arrives as a legacy event (no returnItemsValue), new promotion-service reverses all E again on top of the earlier per-return takes. This can happen when an old order-service instance enqueues the completing refund during a rolling order-service deploy. The over-reversal is clamped to the balance, but it contradicts the brief's 'no double-reverse' check and the runbook line 'Old order-service events still work (legacy path)'.
findings.fix: In onFullyRefunded, take the lock first, then subtract SUM(earn_due) FROM coin_return_reversals WHERE order_id = :o from earned (or return early when any row exists). Add an integration test: a per-return partial, then onFullyRefunded, totals at most E.

findings.issue: The tests do not pin the rounding mode. 25/3, 33/3 and 10/3 give the same result under RoundingMode.DOWN and HALF_UP, so a change to HALF_UP (which breaks 'rounded down', AC-15) would still pass every test.
findings.fix: Seed a value whose third has a fractional part of .5 or more, e.g. N=26 or E=35 (expect 8 or 11, not 9 or 12).

findings.issue: AC-16 exactness depends on the completing return's event carrying paymentStatus=REFUNDED, which comes from completeRefund calling o.fullyRefunded() after markRefunded. Only the negative case (a partial return is not REFUNDED) is checked end to end. The positive case is checked only in a publisher unit test that uses a mocked OrderResponse.
findings.fix: Add an integration case that refunds a return covering all items (or the last of the sibling returns) and asserts that the outbox payload contains "paymentStatus":"REFUNDED" together with returnItemsValue.

findings.issue: The runbook (and ADR 0009) says RETURN_REFUNDED events 'with a returnId' skip the age gate. The code also requires returnItemsValue. That is the correct choice, because old order-service events already carry returnId, but the docs misdescribe the rule.
findings.fix: Reword to 'with returnId and returnItemsValue (new-format events)'.

findings.issue: A non-completing per-return event with a null or zero orderItemsValue silently gets 0 dues. The reversal row is written, but nothing records why.
findings.fix: Log a WARN when orderValue is null or not positive on a non-completing return.

findings.issue: The deserialisation test uses a bare ObjectMapper, not the production KafkaJson.eventDeserializer used by OrderKafkaConfig.
findings.fix: Deserialise through KafkaJson.eventDeserializer(OrderEvent.class, ...) so the test matches the production path.

summary: The change matches design.md and ADR 0009. order-service only adds returnItemsValue and orderItemsValue to the outbox-committed RETURN_* event, so coins stay off the money path. promotion-service onReturnRefunded runs under the per-user advisory xact lock. It checks the coin_return_reversals PK first, so a replay is a no-op, including after a clamp (tested with a top-up before the replay). Dues are floor(X*value/orderValue) with RoundingMode.DOWN, capped at X minus prior dues. The completing return (paymentStatus=REFUNDED, set only by Order.fullyRefunded after markRefunded under lockById) takes the remainder, so totals are exactly N and E in any order (tested with the completing return processed first). Legacy redeem-/earn- rows count as prior. The redeemed give-back is applied before the earn clamp. earn_due and earn_taken are always recorded, a SHORTFALL WARN is logged, and V5 is purely additive (Flyway ignores future migrations on rollback by default). The age-gate exemption applies only to RETURN_REFUNDED with returnId and returnItemsValue; legacy and other events keep the filter, and both cases are tested. Deploy order (promotion first) and the rollback caveat are documented correctly. The remaining gaps are minor: the legacy onFullyRefunded path ignores per-return rows (a narrow mixed-format window, clamped), the floor rounding mode is not pinned by any test, and there is no end-to-end check that the completing return's event carries REFUNDED. No blocker or major findings.
